title: Two-week social calendar under platform and date rules
prompt:
Marlow Cycle Works is running Spring Tune-Up Week. Using only the campaign brief, write the two-week social calendar that leads up to it: twelve posts across X, LinkedIn and Instagram, following every rule in the brief.

Output the calendar first, one line per post, in date order, in exactly the brief's format:

POST <n>: <YYYY-MM-DD> | <X, LinkedIn or Instagram> | <post text>

Number the posts 1 to 12. Put each post's whole text on its own line, with no line break inside a post. After the calendar, add a note of no more than 120 words on how the sequence builds from the first post to the last.

Character counts include spaces, hashtags and links. This is a draft for review; schedule nothing and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: All twelve numbered posts are present in the required one-line format; the first line bearing each number is the graded post.
Exactly four posts are on X, four on LinkedIn and four on Instagram.
All twelve posts are dated from 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-15 inclusive.
All twelve posts are at or under their platform's character limit (X 280, LinkedIn 600, Instagram 400).
No platform has two posts on the same day, and no LinkedIn post falls on a Saturday or Sunday.
All twelve posts carry #TuneUpWeek, and no post exceeds its platform's hashtag limit (X 2, LinkedIn 3, Instagram 5).

skill_adherence.check: No post dated before 2026-03-09 contains a dollar amount or the booking link.
No post dated 2026-03-14 or 2026-03-15 contains the booking link.
Every post that states the $79 price also contains the exact sentence 'Parts extra.'
No post uses the words guaranteed, cheapest or best, or '#1'.
Every dollar amount anywhere in the response is $79, $99 or $20, the only amounts the brief supports.

No post dated before 2026-03-09 hints in words at the price, the saving or where to book (for example 'a special price is coming', 'save on your tune-up', 'link in bio to book'). A dollar amount or the booking link itself is checked separately and is not judged here. Announcing the dates of the week, when booking opens, and what a tune-up covers is fine.

No post dated 14 or 15 March invites people in words to book or says places are still available. The booking link itself is checked separately and is not judged here. Posts dated 9 to 13 March may invite booking.

Every statement about the shop, the tune-up, the price, the dates and the number of slots matches the brief. No invented scarcity or demand (such as 'selling fast' or 'almost full'), testimonials, mechanic credentials, guarantees, extra services or prices.

best_practices.check: The calendar follows the brief's dates in a sensible arc: awareness of the week before 9 March, booking opening on 9 March, reminders before the 13 March close, and something other than a booking push on 14 and 15 March.
Posts for the three platforms differ in more than length: each reads as written for its platform rather than one text trimmed three ways, and no two posts are near-duplicates.
Each post makes at most one ask of the reader.
